Download and extract the ZIP. Keep the extracted folder on your computer.
In Chrome, open Extensions → Manage extensions. Enable Developer mode.
Choose Load unpacked and select the extracted folder containing manifest.json.
Pin Localine from Chrome’s Extensions menu so it is easy to open.
Not listed in the Chrome Web Store yet. Install the ZIP manually for this testnet pilot. No wallet permissions are requested.
Open the demo store, add a product, and continue to checkout. Select a purchase of 15 USDC or less, the current test pool’s per-payment limit.
Keep the checkout tab active. Open Localine and click “Faturayı oku” (Read invoice). The extension reads the active checkout’s invoice from the configured merchant server.

Copy the demo merchant address shown in the checkout and paste it into Localine. Click “Bilgileri doğrula” (Verify details). The address must match the server invoice. Localine does not choose a recipient automatically from the page.
Choose “Yerel ödeme ile devam et” (Continue with local payment). Review the amount, demo rate, and fee. The app reserves pool liquidity before opening iyzico’s hosted sandbox form.
Enter the test verification code displayed by the simulated bank page. Never enter a real card number or a real SMS code.
Example: 3 USDC × 45 TRY + 2% fee = 137.70 TRY sandbox charge. The merchant receives the full 3 USDC. The rate is fixed for the demo, not a market quote.

The order is marked paid only after the provider capture and finalized USDC payout are verified. The worker continues if you close the tab. Keep the private recovery link from checkout so you can return to the order.
A definitive payout failure triggers a full sandbox TRY refund. An uncertain result may require review. Do not pay again while an order is still processing.

Our first merchant pilot will focus on gaming and game-server services, VPS and cloud hosting, software subscriptions, and services useful to travelers. This keeps early validation focused on payments rather than shipping, customs or physical delivery.
Pilot partnerships are planned. We do not yet have a confirmed commercial merchant partner. The ShopinBit-style storefront is an independent demo.

The merchant sets the invoice in USDC. After the local payment is captured and verified, Localine’s prefunded pool transfers the full invoice amount to the registered recipient on Monad. The customer’s local service fee is separate from the merchant’s proceeds.
An authoritative, expiring invoice binds the recipient, token, network and amount.
The shopper manually confirms the recipient against that invoice.
Liquidity is reserved before card checkout starts.
Payment completion requires verified capture and finalized chain evidence.

The current extension supports only the configured demo origin. A production merchant integration would need an agreed server-side invoice interface, a recipient configuration, checkout discovery, payment status reporting and reconciliation. Putting a wallet address on a page alone is not enough.

The existing pool uses trusted server attestations of payment-provider capture. It cannot independently verify a bank payment or prevent a later card chargeback. Fiat settlement, FX, liquidity replenishment, commercial provider onboarding, customer support and risk operations must be established before real-money use.

An early merchant model for digital services, built around clear invoices and verifiable settlement.

Localine has three parts: the Chrome checkout extension, the invoice and local-payment backend, and a single USDC settlement pool on Monad Testnet. The product website you are reading is separate from the demo storefront and does not collect payment details.
Extension → trusted invoice → manually confirmed recipient → hosted sandbox checkout.
Reserve USDC → verify provider capture → settle once → verify finalized receipt and events.
Monad Testnet · chain ID 10143 · native gas token MON · official Circle test USDC with 6 decimals. These tokens have no real monetary value.

The store computes the amount from its catalog. The extension reads the server invoice with an invoice-specific capability, not a shared merchant API key. It does not trust scraped page amounts or automatically select addresses. A signed local quote binds the invoice, recipient, token, chain, amount, expiry, rate and fee.
Paid and expired invoice requests are rejected. Invoice capabilities and private recovery links should not be shared publicly.
Postgres stores the immutable quote, payment attempt, provider payment ID and chain journal.
The durable worker saves signed transaction bytes before broadcast. Retries reuse the same signed transaction.
A callback only returns the browser to the order. The backend independently retrieves and verifies the provider result.
The order becomes paid only after canonical finalized pool state, the settlement event and exact USDC transfer agree.
Definite payout failure can trigger a full sandbox refund. Unknown capture, initialization, refund or transaction outcomes are reconciled or held for review.
TROY / iyzico sandbox in Türkiye; one configured demo storefront.
1 USDC = 45 TRY fixed demo rate, plus a 2% payer fee. No live currency exchange.
Pool test caps: 15 USDC per payment, 100 USDC daily payouts plus outstanding reservations. Availability depends on pool liquidity.
No mainnet payments, real card charges, arbitrary website support, PIX or YAPE integrations.
The operator and backend are trusted for fiat capture. Card chargebacks cannot be prevented by the onchain contract.
